content.title: Reports: Cincinnati native expected to be named next head Louisville men's basketball coach
content.text: Cincinnati native Pat Kelsey, who has guided the College of Charleston to back-to-back NCAA Tournament appearances, is reportedly set to continue his coaching career closer to home.Wednesday afternoon, multiple reports, including Yahoo! Sports' Pat Forde, reported that Kelsey is finalizing a deal to be hired as the next head basketball coach at the University of Louisville.If the deal comes to fruition, Kelsey will take over a Cardinals program that has won just 12 games in two years under Kenny Payne, who was fired earlier this month.Kelsey has spent three years as head coach at Charleston, including taking the Cougars to an No. 18 ranking in last year's AP Top 25.Prior to his time at CoC, Kelsey served as head coach at Winthrop (Rock Hill, S.C.) for nine seasons, winning four regular season championships and making three NCAA tournaments with the Eagles.Over his career, Kelsey boasts a record of 261-122.Kelsey attended Roger Bacon High School in Cincinnati for three years. Kelsey transferred to Elder High School for his senior season in 1993 and was part of the team that won the Division I state championship.Kelsey started his collegiate playing career at the University of Wyoming before transferring to Xavier and playing with the Musketeers from 1995-98.From 2001-04, Kelsey served as Director of Basketball Operations at Wake Forest before becoming Assistant Coach at the school from 2004-09.In 2009, Kelsey returned home as Associate Head Coach for Xavier under former head coach Chris Mack.Louisville has not made the NCAA Tournament in five seasons, the longest tournament drought for the program since the tournament field expanded to 64 in 1985. LOUISVILLE, Ky. —Cincinnati native Pat Kelsey, who has guided the College of Charleston to back-to-back NCAA Tournament appearances, is reportedly set to continue his coaching career closer to home.Wednesday afternoon, multiple reports, including Yahoo! Sports' Pat Forde, reported that Kelsey is finalizing a deal to be hired as the next head basketball coach at the University of Louisville. This content is imported from Twitter. You may be able to find the same content in another format, or you may be able to find more information, at their web site. Sources: Louisville is finalizing plans to hire Pat Kelsey of Charleston as its next coach, ending quite the tortured process.— Pat Forde (@ByPatForde) March 27, 2024 If the deal comes to fruition, Kelsey will take over a Cardinals program that has won just 12 games in two years under Kenny Payne, who was fired earlier this month.Kelsey has spent three years as head coach at Charleston, including taking the Cougars to an No. 18 ranking in last year's AP Top 25.Prior to his time at CoC, Kelsey served as head coach at Winthrop (Rock Hill, S.C.) for nine seasons, winning four regular season championships and making three NCAA tournaments with the Eagles. Over his career, Kelsey boasts a record of 261-122. Kelsey attended Roger Bacon High School in Cincinnati for three years. Kelsey transferred to Elder High School for his senior season in 1993 and was part of the team that won the Division I state championship.Kelsey started his collegiate playing career at the University of Wyoming before transferring to Xavier and playing with the Musketeers from 1995-98.From 2001-04, Kelsey served as Director of Basketball Operations at Wake Forest before becoming Assistant Coach at the school from 2004-09.In 2009, Kelsey returned home as Associate Head Coach for Xavier under former head coach Chris Mack.Louisville has not made the NCAA Tournament in five seasons, the longest tournament drought for the program since the tournament field expanded to 64 in 1985.
